statement: Let n = len(nums). Let imin be the unique index with 0 <= imin < n and nums[imin] <= nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n, and let imax be the unique index with 0 <= imax < n and nums[imax] >= nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n. Put l = min(imin, imax) and h = max(imin, imax). Whenever the function returns a result res, res = the minimum of the three integers h + 1, n - l, and l + 1 + n - h.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: The function returns a result res on every input satisfying the preconditions; it does not fail.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, 1 <= res <= n.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, res >= 2.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume n >= 2, n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Let imin and imax be the unique indices of the minimum and maximum elements of nums, and put l = min(imin, imax) and h = max(imin, imax). Whenever the function returns a result res, res = 2 if and only if at least one of the following three conditions holds: (1) h <= 1; (2) l >= n - 2; (3) l = 0 and h = n - 1.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume n >= 2, n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Let imin and imax be the unique indices of the minimum and maximum elements of nums. Whenever the function returns a result res, there exist integers a and b with a >= 0, b >= 0, and a + b = res such that after deleting the first a elements and the last b elements of nums, neither index imin nor index imax remains; equivalently, for each x in {imin, imax}, x < a or x >= n - b.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Let imin and imax be the unique indices of the minimum and maximum elements of nums. Whenever the function returns a result res, for every pair of integers a and b with a >= 0, b >= 0, and a + b < res, after deleting the first a elements and the last b elements of nums, at least one of imin and imax remains; equivalently, either a <= imin <= n - 1 - b or a <= imax <= n - 1 - b.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Let imin and imax be the unique indices of the minimum and maximum elements of nums. Whenever the function returns a result res, for each x in {imin, imax}, res >= min(x + 1, n - x).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers. Let n = len(nums). We assume 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] != nums[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_deletions(nums) returns a result res and minimum_deletions(rev) returns a result res', we have res = res'.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit signed integers satisfying 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, all entries in [-100000,100000], and pairwise distinctness. Let n = len(nums). Let rev be any slice of length n such that rev[i] = nums[n - 1 - i] for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let imin and imax be the unique indices of the minimum and maximum elements of nums, and let imin' and imax' be the unique indices of the minimum and maximum elements of nums'. If imin = imin' and imax = imax', then whenever minimum_deletions(nums) returns a result res and minimum_deletions(nums') returns a result res', we have res = res'.
preconditions: nums and nums' are two slices of 64-bit signed integers, both satisfying the input constraints: same length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, all entries in [-100000,100000], and pairwise distinct elements in each slice.
